hiw_title: How to Prepare 3ds Max Scene for Unity & Unreal
hiw_lead: A comprehensive guide on optimizing your V-Ray and Corona scenes for OneClick3D automated conversion.
hiw_intro: The converter works with 3ds Max 2025 and V-Ray 7 (lower versions are also supported). OneClick3D aims to support the following features to ensure the best real-time results:
hiw_f1_desc: Standard, VrayMtl, and CoronaMtl are supported. Complex materials are either baked into textures or replaced with a gray placeholder. Simplify where possible.
hiw_f2_desc: Standard bitmaps are preferred. Procedural maps will be baked, which increases processing time and file size. Replace procedurals with bitmaps for best performance.
hiw_f3_desc: Use only the 1st UV channel. The 2nd channel is reserved for lightmapping in Unity and Unreal Engine.
hiw_f4_desc: Basic lights from all render engines, self-illuminated materials, and Emissive GI are supported. Intensity and color may vary in real-time engines.
hiw_step1_desc: The scene is unpacked. All cameras are rendered to create reference images for lighting and material matching.
hiw_step2_desc: The "Black Box" magic happens here. Renders are used as ground truth to adapt 3ds Max lighting for Unity and Unreal.
hiw_opt_1: Instances: Use instances as much as possible, but avoid complex baked materials on small instanced objects like leaves.
hiw_opt_2: Polycount: Objects over 50k triangles will be automatically optimized.
hiw_opt_3: Transparency: Glass and transparent materials are replaced with specialized real-time shaders. Simplify these materials for better results.
hiw_opt_4: Environment: SKY and HDRi lighting in standard slots are fully supported.
hiw_final_note: The output includes builds for all platforms and the original project files, allowing you to make manual adjustments if needed.
hiw_cta_subtitle: Upload your 3ds Max archive and get real-time results in minutes.
